sentences.text: Consequently, the tempo climbed over the road divider and dashed against the car.

He was doing business of mechanical workshop in the name and styled as "M/s. Soniya Industries", at Nigdi, Pune thereby he was earning P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc monthly income of Rs.35,000/- to Rs.40,000/-.
Claimants were dependent on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, they prayed to award a sum of Rs.45,00,000/-with interest @ 18% from the date of the claim, from Respondent Nos.6, 7 and the Appellant.
5) Despite notice, Respondent Nos.6 and 7 did not file their appearance and let the claim proceeded ex-parte against them.
The Appellant resisted the claim by filing the Written Statement (Exh.15).
The Appellant contended that at the relevant time and place, the deceased was driving his car at a high speed and from very close to the road divider.
As a result, the deceased lost his control over the car and dashed the tempo.
It was contended that there was breach of the policy terms and condition.
Therefore, the Appellant is not liable to pay the compensation.
6) Hence, the Tribunal framed the relevant issues.
The claimants presented the evidence of Respondent No.1 on Affidavit (PW1/Exh.18).

Income Tax Officer and Prashant Raghunath Virpud (PW4/Exh.56) to prove the driving license of Respondent No.7/driver of the tempo.
Besides, the claimants have relied upon various documents in the evidence.
No evidence was presented by the Appellant in the rebuttal.
P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.d 7)

In the Financial Year 2009-2010, the income of the deceased was Rs.2,99,298/-, out of which Rs.9,910/- were paid as the Income Tax.

sentences.text: At the outset, it is pertinent to reiterate the concept of 'just' compensation under Section 168 of the Act.
It is a settled proposition, now through a catena of decisions 5. 2022 SCC OnLine SC 1338.
P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc including the one rendered by the Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi that compensation must be fair, reasonable and equitable.
Further, the determination of quantum is a fact- dependent exercise which must be liberal and not parsimonious.

It must be emphasized that compensation is a more comprehensive form of pecuniary relief which involves a broad-based approach unlike damages as noted by this court in Yadava Kumar v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd.

entities.text: Yadava Kumar v. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The discussion in the abovementioned cases highlights that Tribunals under the Act have been granted reasonable flexibility in determining 'just' compensation and are not bound by any rigid arithmetic rules or strict evidentiary standards to compute loss unlike in the case of damages.

Hence, any interference by the Appellate Courts should ordinarily be allowed only when the compensation is 'exorbitant' or 'arbitrary'.
(v) Malarvizhi And Others Vs. United India Insurance Company Limited And Another6.

10) Evidence of AW1 is that the accident occurred as stated above.
To support this evidence, she has relied upon the police 6.
P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc papers.
The F.I.R. (Exh.26) was registered only against the driver of the tempo, who ultimately stood chargesheeted for causing the accident by driving the tempo rash and negligently.
The F.I.R. recorded that at the relevant time and place, the tempo was driven towards Mumbai at a high speed, rashly and in a negligent manner.
As a result, the tempo ran over the road divider and dashed to the car of the deceased, which was heading towards Pune.

This fact itself indicates that the driver of the offending tempo was not at all careful while driving and in fact,
he was driving the tempo ignoring the traffic rules.
Therefore, and considering the principles of res ipsa loquitur, the Tribunal concluded that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driver of the tempo.
There is nothing on record to disagree with the said conclusion recorded by the Tribunal.
Despite opportunity, the Appellant did not examine the driver of the tempo to rebut the said evidence.
As such, adverse inference is permissible.
In view thereof, I hold that the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the tempo.
11) The evidence of AW1 and AW2 is that at the time of the accident the deceased was having engineering workshop business in the name and styled as "M/s. Soniya Industries".
This evidence has not seen enough challenge in the cross-examination.
I, therefore, hold that the deceased was doing the said business to earn his livelihood.

sentences.text: It is true that Tax Returns filed prior to the death would have greater probative value.
However, that does not mean that Tax Returns, if filed subsequent to the date of the accident and death of a person, have to be necessarily discarded.

Section 159 of the Income Tax Act provides that after the death of the assessee, his legal representatives are deemed assessees and the legal representatives of the assessee are liable for tax liability.

Thus, it is not possible to accept that the tax returns filed after the death of the person, in respect of whom, the 7. 2017:BHC-GOA:2 P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc compensation is claimed, have to be discarded The New India Insurance Company Limited vs Smt.Shailaja Santosh Jagdale And Ors on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94455935/

sentences.text: However, the Court will have to be cautious and circumspect while placing reliance on the said Returns.

If the income disclosed in the returns along with documentary evidence in the form of account books/ receipts is found to be cogent and acceptable, nothing prevents the Tribunal from placing reliance on the same.
The question would depend upon facts and circumstances of each case.
In the above context, it must be noted that, the deceased was married and maintaining the family of six members including himself.
The balance sheets enclosed with the I.T. Returns indicate that the deceased was doing his business at Nigdi, which is close to Pune city.
Needless to mention that Pune is one of the biggest cities in India.
As such, living expenses of people residing in Pune is on higher side compared to smaller towns and cities.
In Nandini (supra), it is held that assessment of compensation is hedged with several difficulties.
In the exercise of assessment of compensation, a reasonable amount of guess work is necessary, if not inevitable.
That apart, the Tribunal has not considered the net monthly income at Rs.29,906/-, but Rs.24,174/-.
The evidence of PW3 that the I.T. Returns were verified and the same are genuine, remained intact in the cross-examination.
In this background, the Tribunal was right to hold the net annual income of the deceased at Rs.2,90,088/- (vide P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc Exh.34).

To fortify the conclusion above, I have considered the decision in Dr. Sunil Shankar Patil and Ors. vs. Suhel Shaukat Shaikh and Ors.8,
therein in paragraph 3 (iv), the Division Bench of this Court held that :-
"... The income for the purpose of income tax is to be calculated in accordance with Section 15 to Section 17 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 which has its own calculation and the object is to arrive at the tax on such calculated income whereas the salary as per the salary certificate is what is actually agreed to be received by an employee from the employer and same is based on contractual arrangement between the said two parties.

entities.text: Dr. Sunil Shankar Patil and Ors. vs. Suhel Shaukat Shaikh and Ors.8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For example, capital gains under the Income Tax Act, 1961 is calculated after indexing the cost of acquisition whereas in effect the gain received by a person selling capital asset is simple mathematical calculation of reducing the cost price from the selling price.
There are various such examples to show that actual income received would be different than the income calculated as per the Income Tax.
There are various receipts in the nature of reimbursement on which no income tax is levied.

The Income Tax Act itself recognises that many a times the profits shown in the books of accounts is different and more than the income calculated under the Income Tax Act and therefore the provision in the Income Tax Act is made for levying tax which is known as Minimum Alternative Tax, for eg. Section 115J.
This is only to illustrate that income 8. 2024 BHC-AS:14873-DB P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc computed under the Income-tax Act is not the same as what is actually received by a person.
Therefore, income tax returns cannot be considered as the sole basis for determining the compensation under the M. V. Act.
The Tribunal is required to consider the ingredients of the income as per the contract and it is this income which is to be considered for the purpose of arriving at compensation under the M.V. Act.

This is so because the object of compensation under the M.V. Act is to compensate for the loss of pecuniary benefits and to mitigate hardship which is different than the object of the Income-tax Act which has its own The New India Insurance Company Limited vs Smt.Shailaja Santosh Jagdale And Ors on 9 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94455935/
8 provisions to calculate the taxable income for the purpose of payment of tax.

So, half of the amount of the award has been still lying with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1 was aged only 31 years and Respondent Nos.2 and 3 were aged 7 & 4 years, when they lost the deceased (husband/father).
As such, it is difficult to measure the difficulties faced by them due to the premature death of the deceased.

In the backdrop, having regard to inflation, the devaluation of the rupee and the cost of living, it would not be in the interest of justice to reduce the monthly income of Rs.24,174/- as held above and the consequential amount of the award.
16) It is not disputed that AW1 is the widow, Respondent Nos.2 and 3 are the children and Respondent Nos.4 and 5 are the aged parents of the deceased.
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 were minor.
It is not the case that Respondent Nos.1, 4 and 5 had their own income at the time of the accident.
As such, all the claimants were dependant on the income of the deceased and were entitled for compensation.
The deceased was aged 33 years as per his date of birth 13/09/1976, on the PAN Card (vide Exh.39).
The income of the deceased was not P.H. Jayani 01 fa160.2019.doc of permanent in nature.

Therefore, Mr. Huddar conceded with the submission made by Mr. Takke that 40% of the net annual income should have been taken as the future prospects in accordance with the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others 10 and Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and anr.11, but the Tribunal took it as 50%.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Just because on the date of the accident i.e., 12.08.2008, the Return for the Assessment Year 2008- 2009 had not been filed, cannot disadvantage the appellants,
for the reason that the period for which the Return is to be submitted covers the period starting 1 st of April, 2007 and ending 31st March, 2008.
No income earned beyond 31.03.2008 would reflect in the Income Tax Return for the Assessment Year 2008-2009.
To reject the Return on the sole ground of its submission after the date of accident alone,
in our considered view, cannot be legally sustained.
